The table displays the grade distribution of the $ 30$ students in a mathematics class on the last two tests. For example, exactly one student received a "D" on Test 1 and a "C" on Test 2. What percent of the students received the same grade on both tests?

method.method_draft: Read the two-way table: rows are Test 1 grades A, B, C, D, F and columns are Test 2 grades A, B, C, D, F. Students with the same grade on both tests are exactly the diagonal entries where row label equals column label: A/A = 2, B/B = 4, C/C = 5, D/D = 1, F/F = 0. Add these to get 12 students. From the question text, the class has 30 students. Compute 12/30 = 0.40, so the percent is 40%.

method.method_draft: Use a complement approach. From the image, count students whose grades changed by summing all off-diagonal entries. By Test 1 row: A row changed = 2 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 3, excluding A/A; B row changed = 1 + 3 + 0 + 0 = 4, excluding B/B; C row changed = 1 + 3 + 2 + 0 = 6, excluding C/C; D row changed = 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 2, excluding D/D; F row changed = 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 3, excluding F/F. Total changed = 18. The text gives 30 total students, so same-grade students = 30 - 18 = 12. Convert to a percent: 12/30 = 40%.
